# Email & Messaging Design Guide

## Core Rules

- **Subject line is the headline.** If the subject doesn't earn an open, nothing else matters.
- **First sentence = hook.** No "I hope this email finds you well." Start with value.
- **One ask per email.** Multiple asks = zero responses.
- **Mobile-first length.** If it scrolls past the first screen on a phone, it's too long.
- **Signature signals professionalism.** Name, title, company, one link max.

## Email Types

### Cold Outreach (prospect, first contact)
- Subject: Specific + curious. Reference something real about them. Max 7 words.
  - ✅ "Question about [Company]'s AI security stack"
  - ❌ "Following up on our platform"
- Opening line: Their problem or a relevant insight — not your product
- Body: 3–5 sentences max. Problem → why now → one-line value prop
- CTA: Single specific ask. "15 minutes" not "let me know if you're interested"
- PS line optional but effective for social proof or urgency

### Follow-Up Email
- Reference the last touchpoint in line 1
- Add something new: insight, case study, relevant news — not just "checking in"
- Shorter than the original email
- Re-state the ask explicitly — don't assume they remember it

### Executive Email (CRO/CEO-to-prospect)
- 4 sentences maximum
- Peer-to-peer tone: no selling, no feature lists
- Reference a mutual contact or shared context if possible
- Ask for one specific thing: a meeting, an intro, a decision

### Internal Business Email
- Subject: Action verb + topic ("Decision needed: Q2 forecast approach")
- BLUF first: What do you need the reader to do or know?
- Numbered list for multi-part content
- Clear action items with owners at the end

### LinkedIn Message / InMail
- Max 300 characters for connection request note
- Personalize to something on their profile — not generic
- Connection note: why you want to connect, one sentence
- InMail: treat like cold email — hook, value, single ask

## Subject Line Formulas

| Use case | Formula | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Cold outreach | Question about [specific thing] | "Question about your SOC automation roadmap" |
| Trigger-based | [Event] → thought of [their problem] | "After [RSA] — thought about your team's triage load" |
| Mutual connection | [Name] suggested I reach out | "Ron Chen suggested I reach out" |
| Follow-up | Re: [original topic] — quick add | "Re: [topic]: one more data point" |
| Internal action | [Verb] needed: [topic] | "Decision needed: Northwind close plan" |

## Formatting Rules

- **No walls of text.** Max 3–4 sentences per paragraph. Break more often than you think.
- **Bold sparingly.** Only for the single most important phrase or action item.
- **Bullet lists in email:** Only when listing 3+ parallel items. Never nest bullets in email.
- **Links:** Hyperlink anchor text — never paste raw URLs in prospect emails.
- **Signature:** Name → Title → Company → One link (calendar or website). No quotes, no graphics in cold outreach.
